_doc: Lane-plugin delegation — the single source of truth for which dsh plugins mount WHERE, keyed the same way lane routing keys work: platform (the node's OS) and node (glob vs the runner name). Two seams: 'native-web' primes the env of the runner's own proven web-search mount (run-dsh-agent.sh section 2e — per-job copy + regenerated patch overlay); 'plugin' mounts compose-style (in-tree package copied per-job into the profile module tree + insert-row overlay). The runner consults this at SPAWN time (scripts/lane-plugins-consult.py) — no node env changes, no node restarts, plugins land by landing this file. External sources are materialized to the per-box canonical location by scripts/sync-lane-plugins.sh from the keepalive (after the v1 checkout), so pins advance on tag bump.
_gates: Every entry gates before mounting: platform must match, node glob must match, and the entry's own gate must pass (require_browser: at least one probed browser exists — probed paths must be space-free for the env pin; probe_port: 127.0.0.1:port must answer — engine-dependent plugins mount only where the engine runs). A gated-out entry is a LOUD skip, never a dead mount and never a failed run.
_adoption: Gated like the ADR (2026-08-27): pinned refs, deliberate advancement, smoke before fleet-wide. Manual per-box mounts are the 2026-09-21 incident class — never again.

macos._doc: ctx.web provider 'headless-browser' (issue #293, ADR 2026-08-27). Rode the CI-era cell; the decouple orphaned it — this re-mounts it on every macOS node via the runner's native seam. Canonical source kept by the keepalive sync at ~/.dsh/profiles/node_modules/@local/dsh-web-search-browser (2e's default path).
macos._browsers_note: Space-free paths only (the env pin validates [A-Za-z0-9._/@+-]); Brave/Chrome .app paths carry spaces and stay to the plugin's internal discovery. chrome-headless-shell is the cell-proven renderer (ADR mount notes).

macos._doc: reflex_* session tools — thin client for the Reflex command server in the Gauge host (one engine, many hosts; TCC grants live in the engine). Mounts only where the engine actually answers.
